meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why am I here, Hale, and why did I hear about my son's zero from his phone?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.
Forty minutes in a classroom versus a weekend at home with the play open. Of course they differ. Show me both pieces, side by side.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
The checker was never evidence. What does the version history show, exactly?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn, a written apology, and written confirmation that nothing goes on Owen's record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position and nothing was agreed, so she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the principal if she does not get them; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: Nothing moved her position yet; your September 24 comparison was specific and dated, but she answered with the timed-versus-weekend defence and you had not answered it when she asked what the version history shows.
What cost ground: You never owned that the zero went in before anyone called her, so her first question stayed open and she kept pressing on procedure.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence stayed far from that night because you gave no times from October, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she raises the timed-versus-weekend defence, answer it at once with something she can check, such as the version history entries with their dates and times.
